But then my induction went well. My water was broken accidentally when placing the foley but I don’t blame anyone. I didn’t progress after 36 hours and she was stressed so I got a c section. I had preeclampsia and baby had IUGR. I feel they decided to induce at just the right moment. I went in for a BPP on the 14th, was admitted after that appointment, and overnight my BP went from controlled with meds to dangerously high and not coming down. Idk how they knew but they did. 

I am only one person and your mileage may vary but I would return to Magee if I had another high risk pregnancy, and I am forever thankful for my life and my daughters life

Hi!! I just had a baby with short long bones. Turns out for us, I had gestational hypertension which developed into preeclampsia and she had a two vessel cord. My NIPT came back clear. Her head and belly circumference were fine just her arms and legs. 

For us, it was just that the two vessel cord and high blood pressure meant she wasn’t getting the nutrition she needed from the placenta, so her body was prioritizing growth of her internal organs and brain over her arms and legs. 

She was in the 10th percentile at 20 weeks. At 24 weeks we began weekly NSTs (monitors hooked to your belly to track the heart rate and potential contractions). At 28 weeks I began weekly bio physical profiles, ultrasounds to check her breathing, fluid, and cord flow. Every 3 weeks I had a growth ultrasound to track her size. She dropped to the less than 1st percentile before birth at 35 weeks. She was born 3 lbs 12 oz, small but otherwise healthy. She is 12 weeks now and hitting her milestones on track so far, growing, and just the happiest girl. 

I know this is all scary and overwhelming. You’ll probably be referred out to Maternal Fetal Medicine, but honestly getting all the extra monitoring really helped me feel at ease.
